NEAR's agent economy, measured

NEAR's long-term case is a bet that NEAR Intents becomes the settlement layer for cross-chain money moved by software, including autonomous agents. We test the three halves of that bet separately, from public data only.

Rebuilt by node build.mjs on 2026-11-11T06:40:04.617Z (data through 2026-11-10). Claim and tests: THESIS.md; forward tests: PREREG.md; code and raw data: github.com/tenxagent/near-agent-economy.

What it means for a NEAR holder

Usage moved to NEAR Intents: it settled 83% of NEAR's DEX volume over the last 6 full months and $12.10B in the 90 days to 2026-11-10, 1.84× the 90 days before (T1, T2).

Some of that value reaches NEAR holders, through buybacks rather than protocol fees. Since the fee switch of 2026-02-23, captured Intents revenue buys NEAR on the open market. In the 90 days to 2026-11-10 that was $5.1M, 28% of Intents' fees; NEAR's gas burn added $262.0K (C1). "Buyback" is DefiLlama's label for revenue swept as NEAR into NEAR's revenue wallets, held, not burned; on chain those wallets account for 98% of it, 33% in the front-end fund rather than the buyback multisig.

It is small next to the token. Annualized, captured value is $21.6M, 0.45% a year of NEAR's $4.76B market cap. Over the same months NEAR's total supply grew 2.5% a year net of burns, about $117.0M a year at $3.63; the buyback is 18% of that. The bought-back NEAR is held (2.25M NEAR in buybacks.multisignature.near), not burned. If NEAR governance's HSP-029 cut (max issuance 2.5% → 1.6% over 24 months) runs its full ramp, the same buyback would cover 28% of net issuance.

NEAR's weekly price does not move with Intents volume (r = 0.00 over 96 weeks, T4; with BTC's moves taken out, r = -0.03, p = 0.81, T4m), and agent commerce is tiny next to Intents (T7). Small tickets are not an edge case: 48% of sampled swap legs and 47% of withdrawals were under $50 (P1). Agent-size tickets into NEAR get a 1Click quote: 0.18–0.35% under $50 (T9, quotes of 2026-11-11 06:39Z).

Read as an investment case: the usage half is supported by the record so far (T1 and T2 describe the past; the forward tests F1 and F2 check it on new data), value capture exists but covers about 18% of issuance, and the agent half is still an option. The case for the token is that the captured share grows faster than supply; we would call it made when the buyback reaches half of net issuance over a 90-day window.

Model: when does the buyback reach half of new supply?

Model (`node model.mjs`, every assumption is a flag): starting from today's 18%, when the buyback reaches half of net issuance depends on how fast Intents' growth fades: in 2027-Q2 (2 quarters) if the measured 1.84× per 90 days never fades, and never with no further growth (it stays at 18%). In between: halving every 2 quarters (the default flag), in 2027-Q3 (3 quarters); halving about every 0.9 quarters (the fade a two-point fit to the measured quarters implies, see below), not within 10 years. A scenario, not a forecast. The measured quarter-on-quarter growth went 6.1× → 6.4× → 1.8× → 0.7× → 1.2× → 1.8×; fading from the oldest quarter to the latest four implies a half-life of about 0.9 quarters, but the last 2 quarters re-accelerated (0.7× → 1.2× → 1.8×), so one steady fade fits this series poorly: that half-life is a two-point fit, and the sensitivity grid (`node model.mjs`, and the dashboard's model section) shows how much the choice matters. The bought-back NEAR sits in a multisig (held, not burned); `--resold` models some of it returning to market. If HSP-029 (max issuance 2.5% → 1.6% over 24 months; House of Stake vote 99.97% for, timelock until 2026-11-16; no start date set) began its ramp now: at the 2-quarter default, in 2027-Q3 (3 quarters); at the two-point-fit fade, in 2028-Q3 (7 quarters).

Coverage = NEAR bought back per year ÷ net new NEAR per year. Now 17.6%. The answer depends on how fast Intents' growth fades (the grid below). With the default flag (halving every 2 quarters): 62.6% in 4 quarters, 89.8% in 8. At the faster fade a two-point fit to the measured quarters implies (halving every 0.94 quarters): 33.6% in 4 quarters, 35.0% in 8.

T4LREPORTValue capture

Does Intents volume lead or lag NEAR's own price move (BTC taken out) by up to 8 weeks?

Over 96 weeks, with BTC's moves taken out, Intents volume does not lead NEAR's price at any lag from 1 to 8 weeks (strongest r = -0.09, at +7). The strongest link at any lag is r = -0.27, NEAR's price leading by 3 weeks; it clears the family-wise band (0.21 from all 62 allowed circular shifts of the volume series, p = 0.02) but not on ranks (Spearman -0.23 vs its band 0.28, p = 0.32), so we read it as fragile. Added after the lock; T4 and T4m are unchanged.

Rule: post-lock REPORT (2026-11-09), no threshold: corr(NEAR residual at week t, Intents volume change at week t - k) for k = -8..+8; family-wise p = share of circular shifts of the volume series (all shifts s with 16 < s < n - 16, exact, no seed) whose max |r| over the 17 lags is >= the observed max; the same scan on ranks as a check against a few extreme weeks

C1REPORTValue capture

How much of Intents' usage reaches NEAR holders, next to NEAR's issuance?

In the 90 days to 2026-11-10, $5.1M of Intents revenue bought NEAR back (27.8% of Intents' fees) and gas burn added $262.0K: $21.6M a year, 0.45% of NEAR's market cap. NEAR's supply grew 2.5% a year net of burns ($117.0M); the buyback is 18% of that. Counting only the NEAR that reached the buyback multisig straight from intents.near in the same window (67% of what the series implies), it is 12%, a lower bound. The 50% bar (THESIS.md) is read on the series figure, 18%, as preregistered.

cross-check: The buyback wallet holds 68% of the NEAR the series would have bought at daily prices. Its 3,337 receipts through 2026-11-11 (NearBlocks) close its balance on that day to within 0.015 NEAR (about its own transaction fees): 77% of the NEAR that arrived came from intents.near (first on 2026-04-23) and 23% from 1csfundsadmin.sputnik-dao.near (largest single transfer 502,793 NEAR on 2026-09-09), and 12,025 NEAR left it (largest: 12,000 NEAR on 2026-07-10). So the gap is not outflows: by the end of 2026-04 the wallet had received 4% of the NEAR implied since the fee switch, and by 2026-11-11 (its newest receipt here) 69%. In C1's own window (2026-08-13 to 2026-11-10) this wallet received 102% of the NEAR the series implies, 67% of it from intents.near and most of the rest as one 502,793 NEAR transfer from 1csfundsadmin.sputnik-dao.near on 2026-09-09 (a hop the series counted when the NEAR first reached that fund). The series is not one wallet: DefiLlama's adapter counts NEAR swept into three NEAR revenue wallets and labels all of it "NEAR Buyback" from 2026-02-23. Across all three (balances at the fee switch and on 2026-11-10, archival RPC), the NEAR gained plus the 12,025 NEAR the buyback wallet sent out comes to 3,189,241 NEAR, 98% of the 3,268,478 NEAR the series implies through 2026-11-09. 33% of it (1,070,527 NEAR) is in the front-end fund DAO, fefundsadmin.sputnik-dao.near; the rest reached the buyback multisig, directly or through the 1Click fund DAO.

protocol fee: The contract's own protocol fee is small next to the buyback: intents.near charges 1 pip (0.0001%) of each side's token_in in a token_diff and nothing on transfers, and its fee collector took in about $8.29 a day over the 7 days to 2026-11-10 (archival RPC, 3-hourly balances; a lower bound), about $3.0K a year, 0.01% of the captured value. The swaps that pay it come to about $4.1M a day, 3% of the volume NEAR reports for those days, so most of the reported volume pays no protocol fee (a 1Click swap can settle as transfers alone, as the agent's own did on 2026-11-05).

Rule: reported, not scored (added 2026-10-31 after the lock: the 2026-02-23 fee switch, missed before the lock; see THESIS.md)

P1REPORTAgents

How large are the intents NEAR Intents executes?

From 300 random blocks over 7 days (163 transactions to intents.near): transfer (mostly fee payouts, see THESIS.md) n=204, 85% under $50, 79% under $10, median $0.29; token_diff n=98, 48% under $50, 26% under $10, median $65; withdraw n=55, 47% under $50, 21% under $10, median $68. Agent-size describes the ticket, not who sent it.

Rule: reported, no threshold (cutoffs < $50 and < $10 registered before sampling; THESIS.md)

P2REPORTUsage

Who signs NEAR's transactions, and how many NEAR Intents accounts do signer counts miss?

In 300 random blocks over the 7 days to 2026-11-09, 284 transactions went to intents.near, signed by 7 accounts (the top 3 signed 99%). In the same blocks intents.near's dip4 events named 166 distinct accounts (154 implicit, 3 0x, 9 named; not matched to the transactions, and they include solver legs); 3 of them signed any sampled transaction. Spring 2026, 150 random blocks a week: NEAR carried 34 transactions a block in 2026-03-09..03-16 and 6.3 in 2026-04-13..04-20; kaiching alone went from 26 a block to at most 0.08 (out of the top-12 list), 96.5–96.8% of the drop. Added after the lock; a report, not scored.

Rule: post-lock REPORT (added 2026-11-09 after the lock; a sample, no threshold; THESIS.md)

P3REPORTAgents

What do NEAR Intents and Relay charge on mainstream corridors at $100, $1,000 and $10,000?

On 5 mainstream corridors (USDC and ETH between Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, BSC; one asset per corridor, cost read in token units, BSC's Binance-Peg USDC taken at par), dry quotes of 2026-11-10 03:24Z: every quote cost 0.010%–0.23% of the amount. NEAR Intents was cheaper on 7 of the 14 tickets both venues quoted (3 of 4 at $100, median 0.014% vs Relay 0.039%; at $10,000 0.018% vs 0.020%). 1Click refused $100 on Ethereum USDC → BSC USDC ("Temporary swap limits: minimum swap amount is $1,000"). The same $100 quote was refused into BSC (USDC), into BSC (BNB), out of BSC (USDC) and accepted into Optimism (USDC, HOT Omni), into Polygon (USDC, HOT Omni), out of Robinhood Chain (ETH → Ethereum ETH), so the minimum follows BSC, not NEAR Intents as a whole. Added after the lock; a report, not scored.

Rule: post-lock REPORT (added 2026-11-10 after the lock; dry quotes, no threshold; THESIS.md)
